title: Multitask Learning Can Improve Worst-Group Outcomes
measurement_description: The paper measures worst-group accuracy for a toxicity classification task (using the Civilcomments dataset) across various demographic subgroups, including religious identities. The goal is to evaluate whether the proposed multitask learning approach can ensure more equitable outcomes and improve performance for the worst-faring groups, which include groups defined by religion (Christian, Muslim, other religions).
findings: The paper finds that its proposed regularized multitask learning method improves worst-group accuracy on the Civilcomments dataset, which includes religious subgroups. This indicates that the method enhances fairness by improving performance for the most poorly-performing demographic groups, which can include groups based on religious identity, in the context of toxicity classification.
